accepted.title: Unipotents in all uniformly deformed right-angled Coxeter representations
accepted.text: Let Σ be a finite connected simplicial graph with vertices1,…,n, n≥3. Define W=⟨s₁,…,s_n | s_i²=1, [s_i,s_j]=1 whenever i≠j are not adjacent in Σ⟩. For real d>1 let M_d have diagonal entries1, entry−d on edges of Σ, and0 elsewhere. Define σ_d(s_i)v=v−2(vᵀM_d e_i)e_i on ℝⁿ. Is σ_d(W) free of nonidentity unipotent matrices for every such Σ and every real d>1?

accepted.text: Let Σ be a finite connected simplicial graph with vertices1,…,n, n≥3. Define W=⟨s₁,…,s_n | s_i²=1, [s_i,s_j]=1 whenever i≠j are not adjacent in Σ⟩. accepted.title: Undistorted integral linear embeddings of virtually compact special groups
accepted.text: Does every virtually compact special group G admit an injective homomorphism G→GL_N(ℤ), for some N≥2, whose image is undistorted? Equivalently, is this map a quasi-isometric embedding for word metrics from finite generating sets? Virtually compact special means that a finite-index subgroup of G is the fundamental group of a compact nonpositively curved special cube complex, admitting a local isometry into a Salvetti complex of a right-angled Artin group.

accepted.title: Type-N curves characterize nonpositive curvature of closed aspherical three-manifolds
accepted.text: An element g of Γ is of type N if inf_{x∈X}d_X(x,gx)=0 for every isometric action of Γ on every complete π-visible CAT(0) space X. Here π-visible means that any two visual-boundary points at angular distance π are endpoints of a geodesic line. For every closed connected aspherical3-manifold M, does M admit a Riemannian metric of nonpositive sectional curvature if and only if π₁(M) contains no nonidentity type-N element? Equivalently, does every non-NPC graph manifold contain an essential closed curve whose group element is of type N?

accepted.title: Virtually unipotent elements that fail universal CAT(0) neutrality
accepted.text: An element g is virtually unipotent (VU) in Γ if for every field F and every finite-dimensional representation ρ:Γ→GL_m(F), some positive power of ρ(g) is unipotent; the power may depend on ρ. An element g of Γ is of type N if inf_{x∈X}d_X(x,gx)=0 for every isometric action of Γ on every complete π-visible CAT(0) space X. Here π-visible means that any two visual-boundary points at angular distance π are endpoints of a geodesic line. Does there exist a finitely generated linear group Γ containing a VU element that is not of type N? Here linear means admitting a faithful finite-dimensional representation over some field.
